question: How much can two successive drops from the same finger prick disagree on haemoglobin?
answer: By more than 2 grams per decilitre in some people, enough to move a result from normal to anaemic. Rice University researchers drew six drops in a row from each of 11 donors; haemoglobin, platelets and white cells all varied significantly between drops. Squeezing the finger mixes in tissue fluid. A single drop is a sample of a sample.
move: Before trusting one small sample, see how much the next one differs.
